original_question: Which subtype of congenital disorder of glycosylation is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme that catalyzes the interconversion of mannose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate?

final_qi.question: Which subtype of congenital disorder of glycosylation is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme that catalyzes the interconversion of mannose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate?
final_qi.long_answer: Phosphomannose isomerase (MPI) converts mannose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate and vice-versa. Loss of MPI activity disrupts the mannose supply for N-glycan precursor synthesis and causes the subtype known as Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation type Ib (CDG-Ib).

final_answer.long_answer: Deficiency of phosphomannose (mannose-phosphate) isomerase, the enzyme that interconverts mannose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate, causes congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ib (MPI-CDG). Lack of this enzyme limits mannose-1-phosphate production for dolichol-linked oligosaccharide synthesis, leading to the characteristic hypoglycosylation seen in CDG-Ib.
